explanation: Sparse feature (~0.08% of steps), 95% of mass in the original phase at t=2 (64%) and t=3 (29%); never fires at t=0,1 and rarely in delimiter/copy phases. It responds to a 3-token trigram: the token two steps back is in {o,a,n,f}, the previous token is in {f,o,a} (prev_tok=f 17x lift, o 12x, a 4.5x), and the current input is one of a preferred set of letters (w strongest, then t,x,r,i,p, weaker q,e,s,l,a). Top activations are prefixes like w o f [t], w a f [r], n o f [w], 0 a f [w]: an f preceded by o/a gives the largest values. When only part of the trigram is present (e.g. o f [j], 0 o [i]) activations are weaker. Rare activations on <DEL> after o f / a f, and on copy-phase w after a short prefix. Does not fire on digits-heavy prefixes or at later positions. The 3-way conjunction reaches dev F1 0.61; looser versions have recall around 0.8 but precision below 0.2, which points to a graded hidden-state direction rather than a clean token rule.
